claim: ESCRT-III machinery has emerged as a key player in the regeneration of a sealed nuclear envelope (NE) during mitotic exit through membrane sealing and disassembly of spindle microtubules.
source: Through membrane sealing and disassembly of spindle microtubules, the Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport-III (ESCRT-III) machinery has emerged as a key player in the regeneration of a sealed nuclear envelope (NE) during mitotic exit, and in the repair of this organelle during interphase rupture.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing ESCRT-III's role in nuclear envelope reformation.

claim: ESCRT-III machinery plays a role in the repair of the nuclear envelope during interphase rupture.
source: Through membrane sealing and disassembly of spindle microtubules, the Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport-III (ESCRT-III) machinery has emerged as a key player in the regeneration of a sealed nuclear envelope (NE) during mitotic exit, and in the repair of this organelle during interphase rupture.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on ESCRT-III function during interphase.

claim: ESCRT-III assembly at the NE occurs transiently during mitotic (M) exit.
source: ESCRT-III assembly at the NE occurs transiently during mitotic (M) exit and is initiated when CHMP7, an ER-localised ESCRT-II/ESCRT-III hybrid protein, interacts with the Inner Nuclear Membrane (INM) protein LEM2.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior knowledge and observations in the manuscript.

claim: ESCRT-III assembly at the NE is initiated when CHMP7 interacts with the Inner Nuclear Membrane (INM) protein LEM2.
source: ESCRT-III assembly at the NE occurs transiently during mitotic (M) exit and is initiated when CHMP7, an ER-localised ESCRT-II/ESCRT-III hybrid protein, interacts with the Inner Nuclear Membrane (INM) protein LEM2.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing the CHMP7-LEM2 interaction.

claim: CHMP7 is an ER-localised ESCRT-II/ESCRT-III hybrid protein.
source: ESCRT-III assembly at the NE occurs transiently during mitotic (M) exit and is initiated when CHMP7, an ER-localised ESCRT-II/ESCRT-III hybrid protein, interacts with the Inner Nuclear Membrane (INM) protein LEM2.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about CHMP7's structure and localization.

claim: CHMP7 plays an important role in the dissolution of LEM2 clusters that form at the NE during M-exit.
source: Firstly, we show that CHMP7 plays an important role in the dissolution of LEM2 clusters that form at the NE during M-exit.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1D-E showing persistent LEM2 enrichment in CHMP7-depleted cells.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylates CHMP7 upon M-entry at Ser3 and Ser441.
source: Secondly, we show that CDK1 phosphorylates CHMP7 upon M-entry at Ser3 and Ser441 and that this phosphorylation reduces CHMP7's interaction with LEM2, limiting its assembly during M-phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 3C-D showing phosphorylation of CHMP7 at these sites in mitotic cells.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation of CHMP7 at Ser3 and Ser441 reduces CHMP7's interaction with LEM2.
source: Secondly, we show that CDK1 phosphorylates CHMP7 upon M-entry at Ser3 and Ser441 and that this phosphorylation reduces CHMP7's interaction with LEM2, limiting its assembly during M-phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 4E-H showing reduced interaction between phosphorylated CHMP7 and LEM2.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation of CHMP7 limits its assembly during M-phase.
source: Secondly, we show that CDK1 phosphorylates CHMP7 upon M-entry at Ser3 and Ser441 and that this phosphorylation reduces CHMP7's interaction with LEM2, limiting its assembly during M-phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced sedimentation of phosphorylated CHMP7 (Figure 4A-D).

claim: Spatiotemporal differences in the dephosphorylation of CHMP7 license its assembly at the NE during telophase.
source: We show that spatiotemporal differences in the dephosphorylation of CHMP7 license its assembly at the NE during telophase, but restrict its assembly on the ER at this time.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing advanced dephosphorylation of chromatin-associated CHMP7.

claim: Spatiotemporal differences in the dephosphorylation of CHMP7 restrict its assembly on the ER during telophase.
source: We show that spatiotemporal differences in the dephosphorylation of CHMP7 license its assembly at the NE during telophase, but restrict its assembly on the ER at this time.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing persistent phosphorylation of bulk CHMP7 during NE reformation (Figure 5D-E).

claim: Without CDK1 phosphorylation, CHMP7 undergoes inappropriate assembly in the peripheral ER during M-exit.
source: Without CDK1 phosphorylation, CHMP7 undergoes inappropriate assembly in the peripheral ER during M-exit, capturing LEM2 and downstream ESCRT-III components.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5H and Figure 6C showing precocious clustering of CHMP7 S3A/S441A.

claim: Without CDK1 phosphorylation, CHMP7 captures LEM2 and downstream ESCRT-III components during M-exit.
source: Without CDK1 phosphorylation, CHMP7 undergoes inappropriate assembly in the peripheral ER during M-exit, capturing LEM2 and downstream ESCRT-III components.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 6C showing LEM2 incorporation into CHMP7 S3A/S441A clusters.

claim: A microtubule network is dispensable for ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming nuclear envelope.
source: Lastly, we establish that a microtubule network is dispensable for ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming nuclear envelope.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D showing CHMP7 assembly after nocodazole treatment.

claim: During division, cells undergo a programmed reorganisation of their interphase architecture to allow cyto- and karyokinesis.
source: During division, cells undergo a programmed reorganisation of their interphase architecture to allow cyto- and karyokinesis.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of cell division.

claim: The division phase (M-phase) is set through the actions of key protein kinases such as Cyclin-Dependent Kinase-1 (CDK1).
source: The division phase (M-phase) is set through the actions of key protein kinases such as Cyclin-Dependent Kinase-1 (CDK1) that modify the behaviour of proteins to orchestrate cellular reorganisation (Champion et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on CDK1 function.

claim: CDK1 modifies the behaviour of proteins to orchestrate cellular reorganisation during M-phase.
source: The division phase (M-phase) is set through the actions of key protein kinases such as Cyclin-Dependent Kinase-1 (CDK1) that modify the behaviour of proteins to orchestrate cellular reorganisation (Champion et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on CDK1 function.

claim: The nuclear envelope (NE) is disassembled during M-phase to grant the spindle access to duplicated chromatids.
source: To grant the spindle access to duplicated chromatids, the nuclear envelope (NE) is disassembled and is incorporated into the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) creating a hybrid organelle containing peripheral and transmembrane proteins from both organelles.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of nuclear envelope breakdown.

claim: The disassembled NE is incorporated into the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) creating a hybrid organelle containing peripheral and transmembrane proteins from both organelles.
source: To grant the spindle access to duplicated chromatids, the nuclear envelope (NE) is disassembled and is incorporated into the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) creating a hybrid organelle containing peripheral and transmembrane proteins from both organelles.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of nuclear envelope dynamics during mitosis.

claim: As cells exit M-phase, membranes from the ER/NE hybrid organelle envelope nascent daughter nuclei.
source: As cells exit M-phase, they must regenerate both their nuclei and their NE. Here, membranes from the ER/NE hybrid organelle envelope nascent daughter nuclei, INM proteins recover their NE localisation, spindle microtubules traversing the NE are disassembled and remaining holes in the NE are sealed (Carlton et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on nuclear envelope reformation.

claim: INM proteins recover their NE localisation during M-exit.
source: As cells exit M-phase, they must regenerate both their nuclei and their NE. Here, membranes from the ER/NE hybrid organelle envelope nascent daughter nuclei, INM proteins recover their NE localisation, spindle microtubules traversing the NE are disassembled and remaining holes in the NE are sealed (Carlton et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on nuclear envelope reformation.

claim: Spindle microtubules traversing the NE are disassembled during M-exit.
source: As cells exit M-phase, they must regenerate both their nuclei and their NE. Here, membranes from the ER/NE hybrid organelle envelope nascent daughter nuclei, INM proteins recover their NE localisation, spindle microtubules traversing the NE are disassembled and remaining holes in the NE are sealed (Carlton et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on nuclear envelope reformation.

claim: Remaining holes in the NE are sealed during M-exit.
source: As cells exit M-phase, they must regenerate both their nuclei and their NE. Here, membranes from the ER/NE hybrid organelle envelope nascent daughter nuclei, INM proteins recover their NE localisation, spindle microtubules traversing the NE are disassembled and remaining holes in the NE are sealed (Carlton et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on nuclear envelope reformation.

claim: ESCRT-III has roles in membrane trafficking and cytokinesis.
source: In addition to its roles in membrane trafficking and cytokinesis (Vietri et al., 2020a), ESCRT-III has emerged as a key orchestrator of nuclear envelope sealing during open mitosis (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), the repair of ruptured micro- and parental nuclear envelopes in interphase (Willan et al., 2019; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Robijns et al., 2016; Vietri et al., 2020b) and the surveillance of damaged NPC complexes in S. cerevisiae (Webster et al., 2016; Webster et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work on ESCRT-III function.

claim: ESCRT-III is a key orchestrator of nuclear envelope sealing during open mitosis.
source: In addition to its roles in membrane trafficking and cytokinesis (Vietri et al., 2020a), ESCRT-III has emerged as a key orchestrator of nuclear envelope sealing during open mitosis (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), the repair of ruptured micro- and parental nuclear envelopes in interphase (Willan et al., 2019; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Robijns et al., 2016; Vietri et al., 2020b) and the surveillance of damaged NPC complexes in S. cerevisiae (Webster et al., 2016; Webster et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on ESCRT-III function in nuclear envelope sealing.

claim: ESCRT-III is involved in the repair of ruptured micro- and parental nuclear envelopes in interphase.
source: In addition to its roles in membrane trafficking and cytokinesis (Vietri et al., 2020a), ESCRT-III has emerged as a key orchestrator of nuclear envelope sealing during open mitosis (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), the repair of ruptured micro- and parental nuclear envelopes in interphase (Willan et al., 2019; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Robijns et al., 2016; Vietri et al., 2020b) and the surveillance of damaged NPC complexes in S. cerevisiae (Webster et al., 2016; Webster et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on ESCRT-III function in nuclear envelope repair.

claim: ESCRT-III is involved in the surveillance of damaged NPC complexes in S. cerevisiae.
source: In addition to its roles in membrane trafficking and cytokinesis (Vietri et al., 2020a), ESCRT-III has emerged as a key orchestrator of nuclear envelope sealing during open mitosis (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), the repair of ruptured micro- and parental nuclear envelopes in interphase (Willan et al., 2019; Raab et al., 2016; Denais et al., 2016; Robijns et al., 2016; Vietri et al., 2020b) and the surveillance of damaged NPC complexes in S. cerevisiae (Webster et al., 2016; Webster et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on ESCRT-III function in yeast.

claim: ESCRT-III is a membrane remodelling filamentous polymer.
source: ESCRT-III is a membrane remodelling filamentous polymer that works in-concert with a AAA-ATPase called VPS4 that provides energy for filament remodelling.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of ESCRT-III structure and function.

claim: ESCRT-III works in-concert with a AAA-ATPase called VPS4 that provides energy for filament remodelling.
source: ESCRT-III is a membrane remodelling filamentous polymer that works in-concert with a AAA-ATPase called VPS4 that provides energy for filament remodelling.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of ESCRT-III and VPS4 function.

claim: VPS4 is recruited to ESCRT-III proteins through engagement of sequences called MIMs (MIT-domain interaction motifs) through its MIT (Microtubule Interaction and Trafficking) domain found within ESCRT-III proteins.
source: VPS4 is recruited to ESCRT-III proteins through engagement of sequences called MIMs (MIT-domain interaction motifs) through its MIT (Microtubule Interaction and Trafficking) domain found within ESCRT-III proteins.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of VPS4-ESCRT-III interactions.

claim: During M-exit, the inner nuclear membrane protein LEM2 assembles into a phase-separated gel-like polymer.
source: In the context of NE reformation, during M-exit, the inner nuclear membrane protein LEM2 assembles into a phase-separated gel-like polymer that defines sites of ESCRT-dependent nuclear envelope sealing through its ability to recruit and activate polymerisation of the ER-localised ESCRT-III protein, CHMP7 (Gu et al., 2017; von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on LEM2 function.

claim: LEM2 defines sites of ESCRT-dependent nuclear envelope sealing through its ability to recruit and activate polymerisation of CHMP7.
source: In the context of NE reformation, during M-exit, the inner nuclear membrane protein LEM2 assembles into a phase-separated gel-like polymer that defines sites of ESCRT-dependent nuclear envelope sealing through its ability to recruit and activate polymerisation of the ER-localised ESCRT-III protein, CHMP7 (Gu et al., 2017; von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on LEM2-CHMP7 interactions.

claim: CHMP7 and LEM2 may regulate nuclear envelope sealing by feeding new ER membrane.
source: Furthermore, CHMP7 and LEM2 may also regulate nuclear envelope sealing by feeding new ER membrane, as recently shown in C. elegans (Penfield et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work in C. elegans.

claim: In worms and fission yeast, LEM2 has important roles in stabilising peripheral heterochromatin.
source: In worms and fission yeast, LEM2 also has important roles in stabilising peripheral heterochromatin and in organising chromatin architecture in the interphase nucleus (Ikegami et al., 2010; Barrales et al., 2016; Pieper et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on LEM2 function in other organisms.

claim: In worms and fission yeast, LEM2 has important roles in organising chromatin architecture in the interphase nucleus.
source: In worms and fission yeast, LEM2 also has important roles in stabilising peripheral heterochromatin and in organising chromatin architecture in the interphase nucleus (Ikegami et al., 2010; Barrales et al., 2016; Pieper et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on LEM2 function in other organisms.

claim: CHMP7 and LEM2 are localised to the ER and the INM, respectively, during interphase.
source: CHMP7 and LEM2 exhibit complex domain architectures (Figure 1A) and in interphase are localised to the ER and the INM, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge and observations in the manuscript.

claim: In early mitosis, GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh co-localised in a hybrid ER/NE.
source: In early mitosis, GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh co-localised in a hybrid ER/NE, were then transiently co-enriched at sites of ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming NE, and subsequently adopted distinct ER and NE identities as cells exited mitosis (Figure 1C, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh were transiently co-enriched at sites of ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming NE during M-exit.
source: In early mitosis, GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh co-localised in a hybrid ER/NE, were then transiently co-enriched at sites of ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming NE, and subsequently adopted distinct ER and NE identities as cells exited mitosis (Figure 1C, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh subsequently adopted distinct ER and NE identities as cells exited mitosis.
source: In early mitosis, GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2-mCh co-localised in a hybrid ER/NE, were then transiently co-enriched at sites of ESCRT-III assembly at the reforming NE, and subsequently adopted distinct ER and NE identities as cells exited mitosis (Figure 1C, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: LEM2-depletion prevented the transient assembly of CHMP7 at the reforming NE.
source: As expected (Gu et al., 2017), LEM2-depletion prevented the transient assembly of CHMP7 at the reforming NE (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and is consistent with prior work.

claim: The LEM-domain is necessary for efficient LEM2 and CHMP7 enrichment at the reforming nuclear envelope.
source: We generated cells stably expressing LEM2-mCh or LEM2δLEM-mCh (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and found that the LEM-domain was necessary for efficient LEM2 and CHMP7 enrichment at the reforming nuclear envelope, and subsequent retention of LEM2 at the NE (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and Figure 1—video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The LEM-domain is necessary for subsequent retention of LEM2 at the NE.
source: We generated cells stably expressing LEM2-mCh or LEM2δLEM-mCh (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and found that the LEM-domain was necessary for efficient LEM2 and CHMP7 enrichment at the reforming nuclear envelope, and subsequent retention of LEM2 at the NE (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and Figure 1—video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: In cells co-expressing GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2δLEM-mCh, both proteins co-assembled in the peripheral ER after nuclear envelope reformation.
source: In cells co-expressing GFP-CHMP7 and LEM2δLEM-mCh, both proteins instead co-assembled in the peripheral ER after nuclear envelope reformation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Deletion of the CHMP7-interaction domain from LEM2 (LEM2δ415-485-mCh) resulted in the generation of clusters of LEM2 and nuclear envelope morphology defects in the following interphase.
source: Deletion of the CHMP7-interaction domain from LEM2 (LEM2δ415-485-mCh, von Appen et al., 2020) also resulted in the generation of clusters of LEM2 and nuclear envelope morphology defects in the following interphase (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: LEM2 must effectively gain chromatin tethers during mitotic exit to localise CHMP7 to the reforming NE.
source: These data suggest that LEM2 must effectively gain chromatin tethers during mitotic exit to localise CHMP7 to the reforming NE, and that persistent LEM2 in the peripheral ER can seed inappropriate CHMP7 clustering during mitotic exit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on LEM2 domain deletions.

claim: Persistent LEM2 in the peripheral ER can seed inappropriate CHMP7 clustering during mitotic exit.
source: These data suggest that LEM2 must effectively gain chromatin tethers during mitotic exit to localise CHMP7 to the reforming NE, and that persistent LEM2 in the peripheral ER can seed inappropriate CHMP7 clustering during mitotic exit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on LEM2 domain deletions.

claim: In S. japonicus, Cmp7 disaggregates Lem2 clusters during interphase and mitotic exit.
source: In S. japonicus, Cmp7 disaggregates Lem2 clusters during interphase and mitotic exit (Pieper et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work in S. japonicus.

claim: CHMP7 depletion led to persistent enrichment of LEM2 at the reforming NE.
source: Here, we found that CHMP7 depletion led to persistent enrichment of LEM2 at the reforming NE (Figure 1D, Figure 1E and Figure 1—video 4), suggesting that CHMP7 acts additionally to disassemble LEM2 during M-exit.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: CHMP7 acts to disassemble LEM2 during M-exit.
source: Here, we found that CHMP7 depletion led to persistent enrichment of LEM2 at the reforming NE (Figure 1D, Figure 1E and Figure 1—video 4), suggesting that CHMP7 acts additionally to disassemble LEM2 during M-exit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing persistent LEM2 in CHMP7-depleted cells.

claim: Depletion of IST1 did not lead to persistent LEM2 clusters.
source: Importantly, depletion of IST1, an ESCRT-III subunit with well-characterised roles in nuclear envelope sealing (Vietri et al., 2015), did not lead to persistent LEM2 clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), which is consistent with recent findings from yeast and worms suggesting functional diversity across ESCRT-III components during NE reassembly (Penfield et al., 2020; Pieper et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Persistent assembly of LEM2 in CHMP7-depleted cells led to the formation of NE morphology defects during cytokinesis that persisted into the subsequent interphase.
source: Persistent assembly of LEM2 in CHMP7-depleted cells led to the formation of NE morphology defects during cytokinesis that persisted into the subsequent interphase (Figure 1F and Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F-G.

claim: LEM2 clusters in CHMP7-depleted cells did not incorporate other INM proteins such as LAP1 or Emerin.
source: These LEM2 clusters did not incorporate other INM proteins such as LAP1 or Emerin (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: VPS4 was not recruited to the reforming NE in the absence of CHMP7.
source: VPS4 was neither recruited to the reforming NE in the absence of CHMP7, nor recruited to the LEM2 clusters induced by CHMP7-depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–C), suggesting that the clusters may form as a consequence of impaired remodelling of ESCRT-III.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B-C.

claim: VPS4 was not recruited to the LEM2 clusters induced by CHMP7-depletion.
source: VPS4 was neither recruited to the reforming NE in the absence of CHMP7, nor recruited to the LEM2 clusters induced by CHMP7-depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–C), suggesting that the clusters may form as a consequence of impaired remodelling of ESCRT-III.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B-C.

claim: The LEM2 clusters may form as a consequence of impaired remodelling of ESCRT-III.
source: VPS4 was neither recruited to the reforming NE in the absence of CHMP7, nor recruited to the LEM2 clusters induced by CHMP7-depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–C), suggesting that the clusters may form as a consequence of impaired remodelling of ESCRT-III.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the lack of VPS4 recruitment.

claim: In cells bearing persistent LEM2 clusters, there was a breakdown in nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalisation.
source: In cells bearing persistent LEM2 clusters, we observed a breakdown in nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalisation (Figure 1H) and the localisation of DNA-damage markers to the site of these clusters, suggesting that their formation is detrimental to cellular health (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: DNA-damage markers localised to the site of LEM2 clusters in CHMP7-depleted cells.
source: In cells bearing persistent LEM2 clusters, we observed a breakdown in nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalisation (Figure 1H) and the localisation of DNA-damage markers to the site of these clusters, suggesting that their formation is detrimental to cellular health (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A.

claim: The formation of LEM2 clusters is detrimental to cellular health.
source: In cells bearing persistent LEM2 clusters, we observed a breakdown in nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalisation (Figure 1H) and the localisation of DNA-damage markers to the site of these clusters, suggesting that their formation is detrimental to cellular health (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of DNA damage markers and nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalisation breakdown.

claim: In S. japonicus, Lem2 clusters generated in the absence of ESCRT-III sequester heterochromatin.
source: In S. japonicus, Lem2 clusters generated in the absence of ESCRT-III sequester heterochromatin (Pieper et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work in S. japonicus.

claim: CHMP7-depleted mammalian cells showed diminished HP1 foci.
source: We followed endogenous Heterochromatin Protein 1 (HP1) after CHMP7 depletion and instead found diminished HP1 foci in these cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5B-C.

claim: The HP1 defect was more pronounced in cells exhibiting LEM2-mCh clusters.
source: This defect was more pronounced in cells exhibiting LEM2-mCh clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D) and whilst there were a few remaining HP1 clusters in CHMP7-depleted cells, these did not co-localise with LEM2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5D.

claim: Remaining HP1 clusters in CHMP7-depleted cells did not co-localise with LEM2.
source: This defect was more pronounced in cells exhibiting LEM2-mCh clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D) and whilst there were a few remaining HP1 clusters in CHMP7-depleted cells, these did not co-localise with LEM2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5E.

claim: CHMP7 controls a process of LEM2 dissolution during mitotic exit to allow generation of a normal nuclear envelope.
source: Thus, as well as roles in spindle disassembly (Vietri et al., 2015; von Appen et al., 2020) and membrane fusion (Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), we suggest that CHMP7 also controls a separate process of LEM2 dissolution during mitotic exit to allow both generation of a normal nuclear envelope and proper organisation of heterochromatin during the following interphase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on CHMP7 depletion effects.

claim: CHMP7 controls LEM2 dissolution during mitotic exit to allow proper organisation of heterochromatin during the following interphase.
source: Thus, as well as roles in spindle disassembly (Vietri et al., 2015; von Appen et al., 2020) and membrane fusion (Vietri et al., 2015; Olmos et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2017), we suggest that CHMP7 also controls a separate process of LEM2 dissolution during mitotic exit to allow both generation of a normal nuclear envelope and proper organisation of heterochromatin during the following interphase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on HP1 defects in CHMP7-depleted cells.

claim: CHMP7 contains predicted Nuclear Export Sequences (NESs) in Helices 5 and 6.
source: CHMP7 contains predicted Nuclear Export Sequences (NESs) in Helices 5 and 6 that are thought to limit its exposure to INM proteins, including LEM2, during interphase (Vietri et al., 2020b; Thaller et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on CHMP7 structure.

claim: The NESs in CHMP7 are thought to limit its exposure to INM proteins, including LEM2, during interphase.
source: CHMP7 contains predicted Nuclear Export Sequences (NESs) in Helices 5 and 6 that are thought to limit its exposure to INM proteins, including LEM2, during interphase (Vietri et al., 2020b; Thaller et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on CHMP7 function.

claim: Active NESs are present in helices 5 and 6 of CHMP7.
source: We confirmed the presence of active NESs in helices 5 and 6 of CHMP7 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A to 1C) and demonstrated that transient perturbation of exportin function resulted in nuclear accumulation of GFP-CHMP7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transient perturbation of exportin function resulted in nuclear accumulation of GFP-CHMP7.
source: We confirmed the presence of active NESs in helices 5 and 6 of CHMP7 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A to 1C) and demonstrated that transient perturbation of exportin function resulted in nuclear accumulation of GFP-CHMP7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: Transient transfection of NES-compromised CHMP7 constructs led to sequestration of LEM2-mCh in nuclear and cytosolic clusters during interphase.
source: Transient transfection of NES-compromised CHMP7 constructs led to sequestration of LEM2-mCh in nuclear and cytosolic clusters during interphase, with an additive effect observed upon disrupting both NESs (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Disrupting both NESs in CHMP7 had an additive effect on LEM2-mCh sequestration.
source: Transient transfection of NES-compromised CHMP7 constructs led to sequestration of LEM2-mCh in nuclear and cytosolic clusters during interphase, with an additive effect observed upon disrupting both NESs (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: GFP-CHMP7NES1-&NES2- led to inappropriate capture of LEM2 during interphase in nuclear envelope and cytoplasmic clusters.
source: We were unable to generate cells constitutively expressing GFP-CHMP7NES1-&NES2-, however, by transient transduction of cells with retroviruses driving weak GFP-CHMP7NES1-&NES2- expression, we could demonstrate the inappropriate capture of LEM2 during interphase in GFP-CHMP7NES1-&NES2--positive nuclear envelope and cytoplasmic clusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Trans-nuclear envelope segregation of LEM2 and CHMP7 is essential.
source: These data highlight the essential nature of the trans-nuclear envelope segregation of LEM2 and CHMP7, suggesting the existence of a surveillance system poised to monitor the integrity of this barrier (Vietri et al., 2020b; Thaller et al., 2019) and showing that if this segregation is compromised then LEM2 and CHMP7 can inappropriately cluster.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on NES-compromised CHMP7.

claim: There exists a surveillance system poised to monitor the integrity of the trans-nuclear envelope barrier between LEM2 and CHMP7.
source: These data highlight the essential nature of the trans-nuclear envelope segregation of LEM2 and CHMP7, suggesting the existence of a surveillance system poised to monitor the integrity of this barrier (Vietri et al., 2020b; Thaller et al., 2019) and showing that if this segregation is compromised then LEM2 and CHMP7 can inappropriately cluster.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: If the segregation between LEM2 and CHMP7 is compromised, then LEM2 and CHMP7 can inappropriately cluster.
source: These data highlight the essential nature of the trans-nuclear envelope segregation of LEM2 and CHMP7, suggesting the existence of a surveillance system poised to monitor the integrity of this barrier (Vietri et al., 2020b; Thaller et al., 2019) and showing that if this segregation is compromised then LEM2 and CHMP7 can inappropriately cluster.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on NES-compromised CHMP7.

claim: Clusters of CHMP7δHelix6 that formed during interphase were disassembled upon mitotic entry.
source: When analysing our time-lapse data, we noticed that interphase assemblies of GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 were efficiently disassembled upon entry into the next mitosis, but reformed again during mitotic exit (Figure 3A, Figure 3B and Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Clusters of CHMP7δHelix6 reformed again during mitotic exit.
source: When analysing our time-lapse data, we noticed that interphase assemblies of GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 were efficiently disassembled upon entry into the next mitosis, but reformed again during mitotic exit (Figure 3A, Figure 3B and Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: GFP-CHMP7 and GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 were largely indistinguishable during early anaphase.
source: Indeed, GFP-CHMP7 and GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 were largely indistinguishable during early anaphase (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CHMP7 was phosphorylated upon mitotic onset.
source: By capturing GFP-CHMP7 from interphase or mitotic cells, we discovered that CHMP7 was phosphorylated upon mitotic onset (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Sites of mitotic phosphorylation on CHMP7 were mapped to Ser3 in CHMP7's N-terminus and to Ser441 in CHMP7's C-terminus.
source: We mapped sites of mitotic phosphorylation to Ser3 in CHMP7's N-terminus and to Ser441 in CHMP7's C-terminus (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both Ser3 and Ser441 on CHMP7 conform to consensus sequences for the major mitotic kinase CDK1.
source: Both sites conform to consensus sequences ([K/H]-[pS]-[P] or [pS]-[P]-[X]-[R/K]) for the major mitotic kinase CDK1 and we could detect modification of these sites in immunoprecipitated samples from M-phase extracts using phospho-specific antibodies directed against these CDK1 substrate phosphorylation sites (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and sequence analysis.

claim: Modification of Ser3 and Ser441 on CHMP7 could be detected in immunoprecipitated samples from M-phase extracts using phospho-specific antibodies directed against CDK1 substrate phosphorylation sites.
source: Both sites conform to consensus sequences ([K/H]-[pS]-[P] or [pS]-[P]-[X]-[R/K]) for the major mitotic kinase CDK1 and we could detect modification of these sites in immunoprecipitated samples from M-phase extracts using phospho-specific antibodies directed against these CDK1 substrate phosphorylation sites (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Recombinant CHMP7 could be directly phosphorylated by CDK1/CCNB1 in vitro.
source: We found that recombinant CHMP7 could be directly phosphorylated by CDK1/CCNB1 in vitro and that CDK1-phosphorylation reduced the capacity of CHMP7 to sediment (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: CDK1-phosphorylation reduced the capacity of CHMP7 to sediment.
source: We found that recombinant CHMP7 could be directly phosphorylated by CDK1/CCNB1 in vitro and that CDK1-phosphorylation reduced the capacity of CHMP7 to sediment (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Incorporation of phosphomimetic residues at Ser3 and Ser441 (CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E) reduced CHMP7 sedimentation.
source: Importantly, incorporation of phosphomimetic residues at Ser3 and Ser441 (CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E) reduced this sedimentation (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: M-phase phosphorylations placed by CDK1 restrict the ability of CHMP7 to interact with itself and form sedimentable clusters.
source: These data suggest that the M-phase phosphorylations placed by CDK1 restrict the ability of CHMP7 to interact with itself and form sedimentable clusters.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the sedimentation assay data.

claim: LEM2's C-terminus (LEM2CT) could be co-sedimented with CHMP7.
source: We found that LEM2's C-terminus (LEM2CT) could be co-sedimented with CHMP7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), but its sedimentation with CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E was reduced (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D), suggesting that the CHMP7 assembly formed in these assays could interact with LEM2CT.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Sedimentation of LEM2CT with CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E was reduced.
source: We found that LEM2's C-terminus (LEM2CT) could be co-sedimented with CHMP7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), but its sedimentation with CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E was reduced (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D), suggesting that the CHMP7 assembly formed in these assays could interact with LEM2CT.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: The CHMP7 assembly formed in sedimentation assays could interact with LEM2CT.
source: We found that LEM2's C-terminus (LEM2CT) could be co-sedimented with CHMP7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), but its sedimentation with CHMP7 S3D/S441D and CHMP7 S3E/S441E was reduced (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D), suggesting that the CHMP7 assembly formed in these assays could interact with LEM2CT.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the co-sedimentation data.

claim: CHMP7 could interact well with LEM2CT.
source: Here, we discovered that whilst CHMP7 could interact well with LEM2CT, either CDK1-phosphorylated CHMP7 or CHMP7 S3D/S441D were less able to interact with LEM2CT (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E-H.

claim: CDK1-phosphorylated CHMP7 was less able to interact with LEM2CT.
source: Here, we discovered that whilst CHMP7 could interact well with LEM2CT, either CDK1-phosphorylated CHMP7 or CHMP7 S3D/S441D were less able to interact with LEM2CT (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E-H.

claim: CHMP7 S3D/S441D was less able to interact with LEM2CT.
source: Here, we discovered that whilst CHMP7 could interact well with LEM2CT, either CDK1-phosphorylated CHMP7 or CHMP7 S3D/S441D were less able to interact with LEM2CT (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E-H.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation of CHMP7 reduces both its ability to self-associate and its ability to bind LEM2.
source: These data suggest that CDK1 phosphorylation of CHMP7 reduces both its ability to self-associate and its ability to bind LEM2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the interaction and sedimentation assay data.

claim: LEM2CT induced polymerisation of CHMP7 in vitro.
source: We observed that LEM2CT induced polymerisation of CHMP7 in vitro (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), producing curved filaments with periodicity matching the published dimensions and repeat units of the CHMP7 polymer observed previously (von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: LEM2CT-induced CHMP7 polymerisation produced curved filaments with periodicity matching the published dimensions and repeat units of the CHMP7 polymer.
source: We observed that LEM2CT induced polymerisation of CHMP7 in vitro (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), producing curved filaments with periodicity matching the published dimensions and repeat units of the CHMP7 polymer observed previously (von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and citation to prior work.

claim: CHMP7 filaments were not produced when LEM2CT was incubated with CHMP7 S3D/S441D.
source: Consistent with the reduced interaction between CHMP7 S3D/S441D and LEM2CT (Figure 4G and H), these filaments were not produced when LEM2CT was incubated with CHMP7 S3D/S441D (Figure 4I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: In addition to curved filaments of CHMP7, curved lattices of CHMP7 were also observed, suggesting that both linear and lateral polymeric interactions were induced.
source: In addition to curved filaments of CHMP7, we also observed curved lattices of CHMP7, suggesting that both linear and lateral polymeric interactions were induced (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CDK1-phosphorylation of CHMP7 acts to restrict its polymerisation by suppressing self-interaction and interaction with LEM2.
source: These in vitro data support the hypothesis that CDK1-phosphorylation of CHMP7 acts to restrict its polymerisation by suppressing self-interaction and interaction with LEM2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the in vitro experimental data.

claim: Endogenous mNG-CHMP7 initiated assembly 16.32 ± 0.88 min after CDK1 inhibition in monopolar spindle assays.
source: Following STLC arrest, we found that mNG-CHMP7 initiated assembly 16.32 ± 0.88 min after CDK1 inhibition and polymerised in a wave around the chromatin mass from the spindle-distal to the spindle-engaged face (Figure 5A and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: mNG-CHMP7 polymerised in a wave around the chromatin mass from the spindle-distal to the spindle-engaged face.
source: Following STLC arrest, we found that mNG-CHMP7 initiated assembly 16.32 ± 0.88 min after CDK1 inhibition and polymerised in a wave around the chromatin mass from the spindle-distal to the spindle-engaged face (Figure 5A and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Assembly of endogenous CHMP7 persisted for 2.67 ± 0.22 min.
source: Assembly of endogenous CHMP7 persisted for 2.67 ± 0.22 min (Figure 5C), mimicking the assembly dynamics around the telophase nuclear envelope in asynchronous cells both in duration and in that CHMP7 in the peripheral ER was resistant to the assembly signal.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: CHMP7 in the peripheral ER was resistant to the assembly signal during M-exit.
source: Assembly of endogenous CHMP7 persisted for 2.67 ± 0.22 min (Figure 5C), mimicking the assembly dynamics around the telophase nuclear envelope in asynchronous cells both in duration and in that CHMP7 in the peripheral ER was resistant to the assembly signal.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: In CHMP7-depleted HeLa cells stably expressing siRNA-resistant GFP-CHMP7 (GFP-CHMP7R), CHMP7 assembled with similar kinetics to endogenous CHMP7, initiating 16.93 ± 1.21 min after CDK1 inhibition and persisting for 3.32 ± 0.13 min.
source: In CHMP7-depleted HeLa cells stably expressing siRNA-resistant GFP-CHMP7 (GFP-CHMP7R), CHMP7 assembled with similar kinetics, initiating 16.93 ± 1.21 min after CDK1 inhibition and persisting for 3.32 ± 0.13 min (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, Figure 5C and Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 5C.

claim: LEM2-mCh became enriched at the monopolar nuclear envelope 16.21 ± 2.23 min after CDK1 inhibition.
source: Importantly, LEM2-mCh displayed similar kinetics, becoming enriched at the monopolar nuclear envelope 16.21 ± 2.23 min after CDK1 inhibition, and persisting for 4.11 ± 0.44 min.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: LEM2-mCh enrichment at the monopolar nuclear envelope persisted for 4.11 ± 0.44 min.
source: Importantly, LEM2-mCh displayed similar kinetics, becoming enriched at the monopolar nuclear envelope 16.21 ± 2.23 min after CDK1 inhibition, and persisting for 4.11 ± 0.44 min.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: LEM2-mCh localised more strongly at the spindle-engaged face of the NE.
source: In contrast to CHMP7, LEM2-mCh localised more strongly at the spindle-engaged face of the NE (Figure 5B–C and Figure 5—video 3) before being depolymerised and maintaining NE localisation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Enrichment of LEM2-mCh at the spindle-engaged face is indicative of its phase-separated interaction with microtubules.
source: Enrichment at the spindle-engaged face is perhaps indicative of its phase-separated interaction with microtubules (von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the localization pattern and supported by citation.

claim: Microtubules are dispensable for CHMP7 assembly at the nuclear envelope.
source: We next asked whether microtubules were necessary for CHMP7 assembly by using nocodazole instead of STLC to arrest cells at pro-metaphase. In this case, endogenous mNG-CHMP7 assembled and disassembled at the nuclear envelope with normal kinetics (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B – 1D, Figure 5—video 4), suggesting that microtubules are dispensable for ESCRT-III assembly at this site.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: Endogenous mNG-CHMP7 usually assembled synchronously around the perimeter of the chromatin mass.
source: Interestingly, endogenous mNG-CHMP7 usually assembled synchronously around the perimeter of the chromatin mass (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In cells that were able to form a pseudo-furrow, CHMP7 assembled at the furrow-proximal face before spreading to the rest of the chromatin.
source: However, in cells that were able to form a pseudo-furrow (Hu et al., 2008), CHMP7 assembled at the furrow-proximal face, before spreading to the rest of the chromatin, suggesting that there may be a furrow-directed spatial component to ESCRT-III dynamics at the reforming NE (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Figure 5—video 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There may be a furrow-directed spatial component to ESCRT-III dynamics at the reforming NE.
source: However, in cells that were able to form a pseudo-furrow (Hu et al., 2008), CHMP7 assembled at the furrow-proximal face, before spreading to the rest of the chromatin, suggesting that there may be a furrow-directed spatial component to ESCRT-III dynamics at the reforming NE (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Figure 5—video 5).
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the furrow-proximal assembly pattern.

claim: In CHMP7-depleted cells stably expressing LEM2-mCh, LEM2-mCh was poorly disassembled after nuclear envelope enrichment.
source: Consistent with experiments from cycling cells (Figure 1), in CHMP7-depleted cells stably expressing LEM2-mCh, LEM2-mCh was poorly disassembled after nuclear envelope enrichment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and Figure 5—video 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Persistent LEM2-mCh assemblies did not colocalise with microtubules.
source: These persistent LEM2-mCh assemblies did not colocalise with microtubules, suggesting that they do not form as a consequence of impaired spindle disassembly (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F-G.

claim: Persistent LEM2-mCh assemblies do not form as a consequence of impaired spindle disassembly.
source: These persistent LEM2-mCh assemblies did not colocalise with microtubules, suggesting that they do not form as a consequence of impaired spindle disassembly (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lack of colocalization with microtubules.

claim: Phosphorylation of total CHMP7 at both Ser3 and Ser441 persisted for 20 min following CDK1 inhibition.
source: Biochemical analysis of whole cell lysates from these monopolar spindle assays revealed phosphorylation of total CHMP7 at both Ser3 and Ser441 persisted for 20 min following CDK1 inhibition, with dephosphorylation completing 30 min after CDK1 inhibition (Figure 5D and Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Dephosphorylation of CHMP7 completed 30 min after CDK1 inhibition.
source: Biochemical analysis of whole cell lysates from these monopolar spindle assays revealed phosphorylation of total CHMP7 at both Ser3 and Ser441 persisted for 20 min following CDK1 inhibition, with dephosphorylation completing 30 min after CDK1 inhibition (Figure 5D and Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: ESCRT-III-dependent nuclear envelope reformation occurs in a time period when the bulk of CHMP7 in the peripheral ER is phosphorylated.
source: Importantly, these data suggest that ESCRT-III-dependent nuclear envelope reformation occurs in a time period when the bulk of CHMP7 in the peripheral ER is phosphorylated, and that complete CHMP7 dephosphorylation only occurs after nuclear envelope reformation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the timing of phosphorylation and NE reformation.

claim: Complete CHMP7 dephosphorylation only occurs after nuclear envelope reformation.
source: Importantly, these data suggest that ESCRT-III-dependent nuclear envelope reformation occurs in a time period when the bulk of CHMP7 in the peripheral ER is phosphorylated, and that complete CHMP7 dephosphorylation only occurs after nuclear envelope reformation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the timing of dephosphorylation relative to NE reformation.

claim: Only a minor pool of CHMP7 could be detected in a chromatin-associated fraction during M-exit.
source: Using biochemical fractionation, we found that only a minor pool of CHMP7 could be detected in a chromatin-associated fraction during M-exit (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and we discovered that CHMP7 in this pool was dephosphorylated in advance of the larger extra-chromatin ER and cytosolic pool (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B – 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CHMP7 in the chromatin-associated pool was dephosphorylated in advance of the larger extra-chromatin ER and cytosolic pool.
source: Using biochemical fractionation, we found that only a minor pool of CHMP7 could be detected in a chromatin-associated fraction during M-exit (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and we discovered that CHMP7 in this pool was dephosphorylated in advance of the larger extra-chromatin ER and cytosolic pool (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B – 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B-C.

claim: The pool of endogenous CHMP7 assembling at the reforming NE was not illuminated by the pSer3 CHMP7 antibody.
source: We next raised an antibody that was able to detect pSer3 CHMP7 in mitotic cells and discovered that the pool of endogenous CHMP7 assembling at the reforming NE was not illuminated by this antibody (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D – 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D-I.

claim: Phosphorylation of the bulk of CHMP7 in the peripheral ER persists during M-exit, whereas the pool of CHMP7 in contact with the reforming NE is dephosphorylated in advance.
source: These data suggest that phosphorylation of the bulk of CHMP7 in the peripheral ER persists during M-exit, whereas the pool of CHMP7 in contact with the reforming NE is dephosphorylated in advance.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the fractionation and antibody staining data.

claim: CHMP7 bearing non-phosphorylatable residues at positions 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A) assembled at the NE with similar kinetics and intensity to GFP-CHMP7R.
source: We found that CHMP7 bearing non-phosphorylatable residues at positions 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A) assembled at the NE with similar kinetics and intensity to GFP-CHMP7R, but displayed limited precocious clustering on the peripheral ER during early M-phase (Figure 5F–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A displayed limited precocious clustering on the peripheral ER during early M-phase.
source: We found that CHMP7 bearing non-phosphorylatable residues at positions 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A) assembled at the NE with similar kinetics and intensity to GFP-CHMP7R, but displayed limited precocious clustering on the peripheral ER during early M-phase (Figure 5F–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-B.

claim: During telophase, precocious clusters of GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A grew larger.
source: During telophase, these precocious clusters of GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A grew larger (Figure 5H, Figure 5—video 7) and similarly to the clusters induced by GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 or LEM2δLEM, incorporated ESCRT-III components and persisted into the next interphase (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Precocious clusters of GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A incorporated ESCRT-III components and persisted into the next interphase.
source: During telophase, these precocious clusters of GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A grew larger (Figure 5H, Figure 5—video 7) and similarly to the clusters induced by GFP-CHMP7δHelix6 or LEM2δLEM, incorporated ESCRT-III components and persisted into the next interphase (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: M-phase phosphorylation of CHMP7 acts to suppresses its inappropriate assembly on the peripheral ER during both M-phase and M-exit.
source: These data suggest that M-phase phosphorylation of CHMP7 acts to suppresses its inappropriate assembly on the peripheral ER during both M-phase and M-exit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on CHMP7 S3A/S441A.

claim: CHMP7 bearing phosphomimetic residues at position 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D) showed reduced assembly at the reforming NE.
source: We next examined the behaviour of CHMP7 bearing phosphomimetic residues at position 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D) and were surprised to find that these mutations reduced, although did not eliminate, its assembly at the reforming NE (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: Phosphomimetic mutations at positions 3 and 441 did not eliminate CHMP7 assembly at the reforming NE.
source: We next examined the behaviour of CHMP7 bearing phosphomimetic residues at position 3 and 441 (GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D) and were surprised to find that these mutations reduced, although did not eliminate, its assembly at the reforming NE (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D was recruited later than WT CHMP7 during M-exit.
source: Using the degree of cleavage furrow ingression at the point of maximal recruitment as a proxy for progression through M-phase, we found that the residual GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D was recruited later than WT CHMP7 (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Incorporation of phosphomimetic residues at Ser3 and Ser441 limits CHMP7 assembly at the reforming NE.
source: These data suggest that incorporation of phosphomimetic residues at Ser3 and Ser441 limits its assembly at the reforming NE.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on CHMP7 S3D/S441D.

claim: HA-CHMP7R S3D/S441D and HA-CHMP7R S3E/S441E could rescue both the clustering of LEM2 and the nuclear compartmentalisation breakdown induced by CHMP7 depletion.
source: Consistent with a limited assembly of GFP-CHMP7R S3D/S441D at the reforming NE, we found that like HA-CHMP7R, HA-CHMP7R S3D/S441D, and HA-CHMP7R S3E/S441E could rescue both the clustering of LEM2 and the nuclear compartmentalisation breakdown induced by CHMP7 depletion (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: In CHMP7-depleted cells expressing HA-CHMP7R S3A/S441A, cytoplasmic and NE clusters of LEM2 persisted.
source: Importantly, in CHMP7-depleted cells expressing HA-CHMP7R S3A/S441A, cytoplasmic and NE clusters of LEM2 persisted, and the nuclear compartmentalisation defect induced by CHMP7-depletion was only partially rescued (Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: The nuclear compartmentalisation defect induced by CHMP7-depletion was only partially rescued by HA-CHMP7R S3A/S441A.
source: Importantly, in CHMP7-depleted cells expressing HA-CHMP7R S3A/S441A, cytoplasmic and NE clusters of LEM2 persisted, and the nuclear compartmentalisation defect induced by CHMP7-depletion was only partially rescued (Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In CHMP7-depleted cells stably expressing both LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A, LEM2-mCh was incorporated into precocious GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A-positive clusters that formed during M-exit.
source: In CHMP7-depleted cells stably expressing both LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A, LEM2-mCh was incorporated into precocious GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A-positive clusters that formed during M-exit (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A-positive clusters displayed fusogenic behaviour.
source: These clusters displayed fusogenic behaviour (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and Figure 6—video 2) and long-term culture of cells bearing LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A resulted in the loss of LEM2 from the INM with its retention in singular extra-nuclear clusters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Long-term culture of cells bearing LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A resulted in the loss of LEM2 from the INM with its retention in singular extra-nuclear clusters.
source: These clusters displayed fusogenic behaviour (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and Figure 6—video 2) and long-term culture of cells bearing LEM2-mCh and GFP-CHMP7R S3A/S441A resulted in the loss of LEM2 from the INM with its retention in singular extra-nuclear clusters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: CDK1-phosphorylation of CHMP7 is a mechanism to restrict polymerisation and precocious capture of LEM2 in the peripheral ER during mitotic exit.
source: These data highlight CDK1-phosphorylation of CHMP7 as a mechanism to restrict polymerisation and precocious capture of LEM2 in the peripheral ER during mitotic exit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on CHMP7 phosphorylation mutants.

claim: Advanced dephosphorylation of CHMP7 in a chromatin associated pool licenses its polymerisation, ensuring that the nucleus reforms with, and retains, its proper complement of INM proteins for the following interphase.
source: Further, they suggest that advanced dephosphorylation of CHMP7 in a chromatin associated pool licenses its polymerisation, ensuring that the nucleus reforms with, and retains, its proper complement of INM proteins for the following interphase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on spatiotemporal dephosphorylation.

claim: Mitotic phosphorylation of the ESCRT-III components IST1 and CHMP4C regulates cytokinetic abscission.
source: Mitotic phosphorylation of the ESCRT-III components IST1 and CHMP4C is already known to regulate cytokinetic abscission (Carlton et al., 2012; Capalbo et al., 2012; Caballe et al., 2015), suggesting that this machinery is capable of being modified by phosphorylation, and mitotic phosphorylation of LEM2 can control both its interaction with partner proteins such as Barrier to Autointegration Factor (BAF) (Asencio et al., 2012) and its phase-separation properties (von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on ESCRT-III phosphorylation.

claim: Mitotic phosphorylation of LEM2 can control both its interaction with partner proteins such as Barrier to Autointegration Factor (BAF) and its phase-separation properties.
source: Mitotic phosphorylation of the ESCRT-III components IST1 and CHMP4C is already known to regulate cytokinetic abscission (Carlton et al., 2012; Capalbo et al., 2012; Caballe et al., 2015), suggesting that this machinery is capable of being modified by phosphorylation, and mitotic phosphorylation of LEM2 can control both its interaction with partner proteins such as Barrier to Autointegration Factor (BAF) (Asencio et al., 2012) and its phase-separation properties (von Appen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on LEM2 phosphorylation.

claim: CHMP7 is the only ESCRT-III subunit to bear recognisable consensus sequences for CDK1 phosphorylation.
source: Interestingly, CHMP7 is the only ESCRT-III subunit to bear recognisable consensus sequences for CDK1 phosphorylation, suggesting that mitotic regulation of ESCRT-III may be effected through this protein.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis of ESCRT-III subunits.

claim: Phosphomimetic residues at the CDK1-phosphorylation sites suppressed CHMP7's interaction with LEM2 in a minimal in vitro system.
source: Whilst phosphomimetic residues at the CDK1-phosphorylation sites suppressed CHMP7's interaction with LEM2 and reduced its sedimentation in a minimal in vitro system, their effect in cells were more complex to interpret, as we found that CHMP7 bearing phosphomimetic mutations could still be recruited, albeit with a reduced intensity and in a delayed manner, to the reforming NE, and could still rescue the phenotypes of CHMP7-depletion.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro experimental data.
